title: Downhill Running: What Are The Effects and How Can We Adapt? A Narrative Review
claims: Downhill running is a whole-body eccentric exercise model that accentuates exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) and can reduce subsequent running performance.

In reviewed studies, EIMD after downhill running was assessed through isometric maximal voluntary contraction, blood creatine kinase and delayed onset muscle soreness, with slope, exercise duration and running speed as the main influencing factors.
The median downhill protocol across reviewed studies was -12% slope (25th-75th percentile -15% to -10%), 40 min duration (30-45 min) and 11.3 km/h speed (9.8-12.9 km/h).
Runners least accustomed to downhill running generally experienced the most EIMD, and prior exposure to downhill running is the preventive strategy with the strongest supporting evidence.
The review states that evidence for in-situ strategies such as compression garments and specific footwear to limit downhill muscle damage remains unconfirmed.
